correctness.rationale: Full reconstruction of 24-vertex/36-edge/girth-7 McGee graph and its 34304 nonempty independent faces; all 17151 codimension-one matched pairs and the exact critical 0-cell and 5-cell checked; all 197768 oriented face-incidence edges are acyclic by complete topological sort. The resulting CW complex with only a 0-cell and 5-cell is \(S^5\). Independent fixed-cardinality, deletion-recurrence and mod-two boundary computations corroborate all counts and the fifth Betti rank. This is an exact finite proof via discrete Morse theory, not an inference from experiments alone.

evidence: Barmak, arXiv:1007.0418v1, Theorems 3.4–3.5: triangle-free implies a suspension, without determining that it is \(S^5\).
Kim, arXiv:2101.07131v3, Theorem 1.1: requires no induced cycle of length divisible by 3; verified induced 9-cycle (0,1,8,7,6,18,17,16,23) excludes the hypothesis.

Goyal–Shukla–Singh, doi:10.55016/ojs/cdm.v16i3.71284, Sections 3–5, concern categorical products of complete graphs and generalized Mycielskians of complete graphs, plus a particular perturbation operation; the stated family calculations do not identify this cage.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general suspension theorem is strictly weaker than the particular sphere and its dimension. The ternary theorem is inapplicable because a concrete induced 9-cycle violates its necessary hypothesis. For a categorical product of two complete graphs to have 24 vertices, degrees would be 11,14, or 15, never 3; for a generalized Mycielskian of a complete graph with parameters at least 2, the vertex count would be rn+1 and cannot be 24 because 23 is prime. No stronger applicable result was identified.

originality.rationale: No covering McGee independence-complex classification identified in targeted graph, cage, complement-clique, homology and homotopy searches or distinct earlier findings. The closest general theorem gives only a suspension (Barmak); a more restrictive sphere theorem cannot apply due to a verified induced 9-cycle (Kim); explicit complete-graph product and Mycielskian classifications concern different graphs (Goyal et al.). Distinct Heawood and dodecahedral complexes do not logically cover the 24-vertex McGee graph. Residual risk of unindexed equivalent work persists.

value.rationale: The McGee graph is the unique cubic (3,7)-cage, a canonical girth extremizer. A natural exact homotopy type of its nine-dimensional independence complex had not been derived from inspected literature; the result identifies it with one five-sphere by a reproducible 17151-pair discrete-Morse certificate. The conclusion is strictly stronger than a face-count table, characteristic, suspension property, or mod-two homology and offers a precise meaningful finite topological benchmark, without requiring an unjustified family-wide statement.
